rationale: C10 plausibly supplied a material template for the child. Both proclamations concern observance of a congressionally designated civic-law day and combine the same distinctive operative machinery: public observance through appropriate ceremonies, participation by governmental and civic/educational organizations, cultivation of appreciation for constitutional rights and responsibilities, and display of the flag on government buildings. C15 is very similar but somewhat less likely because C10 is the later refinement of that Citizenship Day form. C07 has a close three-part observance, organizational-participation, and flag-display structure, but its substantive connection to constitutional education is weaker.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the Congress of the United States, by a joint resolution approved April 7, 1961 ... has designated the first day of May of each year as Law Day, U.S.A. ... and has requested the President to issue a proclamation calling for appropriate observance of that day
shared_material.parent_excerpt: by joint resolution approved February 29, 1952 ... the Congress of the United States has designated the 17th day of September of each year as Citizenship Day ... [and] authorizes the President to issue annually a proclamation ... for the observance of Citizenship Day with appropriate ceremonies
shared_material.explanation: Both use a congressional annual designation and request for a presidential proclamation to introduce a civic observance grounded in constitutional principles.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I especially urge that the schools, civic and service organizations, public bodies, the legal profession and the media of information participate in this worthy educational undertaking.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I also urge Federal, State and local officials, as well as religious, civic, patriotic, educational, and other organizations, to arrange for appropriate ceremonies on Citizenship Day, in schools and churches and other appropriate places
shared_material.explanation: The child closely adapts the parent's coordinated appeal to public officials, civic and educational organizations, and schools to conduct appropriate observances.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I also call upon public officials to cause the flag of the United States to be displayed on all government buildings on that day.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: call upon the appropriate officials of the Government to display the flag of the United States on all Government buildings on Saturday, September 17, 1955
shared_material.explanation: This is a close literal and functional match in the flag-display instruction, with only the date and formulation of the responsible officials changed.
